chapters.title: Hangul, Syllable Blocks, And Sound
chapters.goal: Get comfortable seeing Hangul as sound blocks, not English letters in disguise.
chapters.scenario: A first quiet study session where the learner reads one block, hears it, and repeats it back.

dialogue.speaker: Tutor
dialogue.en: Today we'll look at just one character. It's 한.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.ko: 한... 천천히 한 번만 더 말해 주세요.
dialogue.romanization: han... cheoncheonhi han beonman deo malhae juseyo.
dialogue.en: Han... please say it slowly one more time.

dialogue.speaker: Tutor
dialogue.ko: 좋아요. 한은 ㅎ, ㅏ, ㄴ이 같이 있어요.
dialogue.romanization: joayo. haneun hieut, a, nieuni gachi isseoyo.
dialogue.en: Good. 한 has ㅎ, ㅏ, and ㄴ together.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Ah, now I'll look at the Hangul first.

chapters.guidedPractice: Break 한글 into blocks, read each block from Hangul, then check romanization only after you try.
chapters.realLifeTask: Ask someone to say one Korean word slowly, then read the Hangul before checking romanization.
chapters.friendPractice: Friend says three phrases from this chapter. Learner points to the Hangul and repeats.
chapters.review: Can you explain that 한 is ㅎ + ㅏ + ㄴ, read a simple block, and use romanization only as a helper?

beginnerGuide.title: What a complete beginner should notice
beginnerGuide.body: Hangul is not an alphabet written in a line like English. Korean letters are grouped into square syllable blocks, so 한 is one spoken chunk made from ㅎ, ㅏ, and ㄴ.

beginnerGuide.title: How to study this chapter
beginnerGuide.body: Look at the Hangul first, try to read it, then use romanization only to check. If you start from romanization, you will build English pronunciation habits that are hard to undo.

beginnerGuide.title: Minimum outcome
beginnerGuide.body: You do not need perfect pronunciation yet. You should be able to point to a block, name its parts, and repeat a short phrase after listening.

checkpoints: I can see 한 as ㅎ + ㅏ + ㄴ.
I can ask 천천히 한 번만 더 말해 주세요.
I check Hangul first and use romanization only as backup.

chapters.title: Greetings And Self-Introduction
chapters.goal: Start a first meeting politely and say your name without freezing.
chapters.scenario: A language exchange table where two people meet for the first time.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Hello. Nice to meet you for the first time.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Hello. I'm Hana.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: I'm Minjun. Nice to meet you.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Nice to meet you too. I look forward to studying together.

chapters.guidedPractice: Replace the name in 저는 하나예요 with your own name, then add one greeting and one closing.
chapters.realLifeTask: Say hello, give your name, and close with one polite friendly line.
chapters.friendPractice: Friend asks 이름이 뭐예요? Learner answers with 저는 ___예요.
chapters.review: Can you greet, say your name, thank someone, and close the conversation politely?

beginnerGuide.title: Why greetings come before grammar
beginnerGuide.body: A beginner needs phrases that work immediately. 안녕하세요, 감사합니다, 죄송합니다, 네, and 아니요 let you participate politely before you can build long sentences.

beginnerGuide.title: Politeness first
beginnerGuide.body: Use polite everyday Korean until the other person clearly uses casual speech with you. This course treats 해요체 and polite chunks as your default safety zone.

beginnerGuide.title: Your first personal sentence
beginnerGuide.body: 저는 ___예요 is not just translation practice. It teaches 은/는 as “as for me,” which becomes the base for many later sentences.

checkpoints: I can say 안녕하세요 without looking at English.
I can say 저는 ___예요 with my own name.
I can close a first meeting with 만나서 반가워요 or 잘 부탁드려요.

chapters.title: Noun Sentences: N이에요/예요 And 은/는
chapters.goal: Point at people and things around you and say what they are.
chapters.scenario: A cafe table with a menu, a notebook, and two people introducing themselves.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: What is this?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: This is a menu. That is my notebook.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: I'm a student. What about you, Hana?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: I'm an office worker.

chapters.guidedPractice: Make three N이에요/예요 sentences: your name, your role, and one object.
chapters.realLifeTask: Use 이건/저는 and say two noun sentences about your table or yourself.
chapters.friendPractice: Friend points to an object. Learner asks 이건 뭐예요? and repeats the answer.
chapters.review: Can you choose 이에요 vs 예요 and use 저는 naturally?

beginnerGuide.title: The first sentence engine
beginnerGuide.body: N이에요/예요 lets you say what something is. This is the noun-sentence engine for names, jobs, objects, places, and simple identity.

beginnerGuide.title: Topic marker in plain English
beginnerGuide.body: 은/는 marks what we are talking about. In 저는 학생이에요, Korean first says “as for me,” then gives the information.

beginnerGuide.title: Do not over-translate particles
beginnerGuide.body: Particles often do not become separate English words. Learn the Korean frame and the sentence job, not a one-word English translation.

checkpoints: I can ask 이건 뭐예요?
I can choose 이에요 or 예요 from the noun ending.
I can use 저는 to set myself as the topic.

chapters.title: Existence And Possession: 있어요/없어요 And 이/가
chapters.goal: Ask what exists, say what you have, and say what is missing.
chapters.scenario: A small restaurant visit where the learner asks about seats and reservations.

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.en: Do you have a reservation?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: No, I don't have a reservation. Is there a seat?

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.en: Yes, there is a seat by the window.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Great. I have time too.

chapters.guidedPractice: Practice 시간이 있어요, 시간이 없어요, 예약이 있어요, 예약이 없어요.
chapters.realLifeTask: Ask whether there is a seat, bathroom, or reservation, then answer with 있어요 or 없어요.
chapters.friendPractice: Friend asks 시간이 있어요? Learner answers with 있어요 or 없어요 and one reason.
chapters.review: Can you use 이/가 with 있어요 and 없어요?

beginnerGuide.title: Existence covers more than “there is”
beginnerGuide.body: 있어요 and 없어요 also mean “I have” and “I do not have.” 시간이 있어요 can mean “there is time” or “I have time.”

beginnerGuide.title: Why 이/가 appears here
beginnerGuide.body: The thing that exists, does not exist, hurts, or appears is usually marked with 이/가: 시간이 있어요, 문제가 없어요, 머리가 아파요.

beginnerGuide.title: Survival value
beginnerGuide.body: This chapter gives you high-frequency travel and daily phrases: 예약이 있어요, 시간이 없어요, 화장실이 있어요?

checkpoints: I can ask 자리 있어요? or 화장실 있어요?
I can say 예약이 없어요 without using 을/를.
I can use 이/가 for the thing that exists or is missing.

chapters.title: Daily Actions: Present Tense And 을/를
chapters.goal: Talk about simple daily actions and the thing you do them to.
chapters.scenario: A morning check-in about breakfast, coffee, studying, and reading.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Are you eating breakfast today?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Yes, I eat breakfast and drink coffee.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Are you studying Korean again today?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Yes. At night I read a little.

chapters.guidedPractice: Make three present-tense sentences with 을/를, then make one negative sentence.
chapters.realLifeTask: Say two things you do today and one object you use with 을/를.
chapters.friendPractice: Friend asks 뭐 해요? Learner answers with one object sentence.
chapters.review: Can you use 먹어요, 마셔요, 공부해요, and 안 해요 naturally?

beginnerGuide.title: From words to actions
beginnerGuide.body: This chapter turns verbs into simple sentences: 밥을 먹어요, 커피를 마셔요, 한국어를 공부해요. The object marker 을/를 shows what receives the action.

beginnerGuide.title: Particle dropping comes later
beginnerGuide.body: Koreans often drop 을/를 in speech, but beginners should first understand the full frame. Once the structure is clear, natural short speech becomes easier.

beginnerGuide.title: Negatives start here
beginnerGuide.body: 안 먹어요 and 공부 안 해요 show the everyday short negative. This means “I do not do it,” not necessarily “I cannot.”

checkpoints: I can say 먹어요, 마셔요, 공부해요, and 읽어요.
I can add 을/를 when the action has an object.
I can connect two daily actions with 고.

chapters.title: Places And Time: 에 And 에서
chapters.goal: Say where you go and where something happens without mixing up 에 and 에서.
chapters.scenario: A simple plan to go to a cafe and meet a friend there.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Where are you going today?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: I'm going to a cafe.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: What are you doing at the cafe?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: I'm meeting a friend at the cafe.

chapters.guidedPractice: Contrast 학교에 가요 with 학교에서 공부해요. Do not mix destination and action place.
chapters.realLifeTask: Say one place you go to and one thing you do there.
chapters.friendPractice: Friend asks 어디에 가요? and 어디에서 공부해요? Learner answers both.
chapters.review: Can you choose 에 vs 에서 in simple sentences?

beginnerGuide.title: The 에 / 에서 split
beginnerGuide.body: 에 points to destination, time, or where something exists. 에서 marks where an action happens. 학교에 가요 and 학교에서 공부해요 are different for a reason.

beginnerGuide.title: Movement vs action
beginnerGuide.body: If the verb is 가다 or 오다, think destination: 에. If the verb is 공부하다, 일하다, 먹다, 기다리다, or 사다, think action place: 에서.

beginnerGuide.title: Time also uses 에
beginnerGuide.body: For clock time, use 에: 7시에 일어나요. Some time words like 오늘, 내일, 지금 usually do not need 에 at beginner level.

checkpoints: I can use 에 for the destination: 카페에 가요.
I can use 에서 for the action place: 카페에서 만나요.
I can avoid 카페에서 가요 when I mean going to the cafe.

chapters.title: Food And Shopping
chapters.goal: Order something small and pay without overthinking the sentence.
chapters.scenario: A cafe counter where the learner orders a drink and asks about card payment.

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.en: Would you like to order?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: One Americano, please.

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.en: Would you like it hot?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Yes. And is card payment okay?

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.en: Yes, card is okay.

chapters.guidedPractice: Practice N 주세요, 이것만 주세요, 이것도 주세요, 카드 돼요?, and 카드로 결제할 수 있어요?
chapters.realLifeTask: Order one drink or food item and ask if card payment is okay.
chapters.friendPractice: Friend plays staff. Learner orders, asks price, and chooses payment.
chapters.review: Can you ask for an item and use 로/으로 for payment?

beginnerGuide.title: Ordering is chunk-based
beginnerGuide.body: In a cafe or store, N 주세요 is more useful than a full English-style sentence. 아메리카노 한 잔 주세요, 빵도 하나 주세요, and 이것만 주세요 are complete practical requests.

beginnerGuide.title: Payment language
beginnerGuide.body: 카드 돼요? is a common spoken shortcut. 카드로 결제할 수 있어요? is clearer and more textbook-complete. Both are useful, but they feel different.

beginnerGuide.title: Small particles, big meaning
beginnerGuide.body: 도 means also, 만 means only, and 로/으로 can show method such as payment or transportation. These small pieces change the shopping situation.

checkpoints: I can order with N 주세요.
I can use one counter like 한 잔 or 하나.
I can ask 카드 돼요? in a simple shop situation.

chapters.title: Want, Can, Cannot
chapters.goal: Say what you want, what you can do, and what you cannot do today.
chapters.scenario: Two friends trying to choose food and make a small plan.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: What do you want to eat today?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: I want to eat bibimbap.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Then can you go now?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 지금은 못 가요. 한 시간 후에 갈 수 있어요.
dialogue.romanization: jigeumeun mot gayo. han sigan hue gal su isseoyo.
dialogue.en: I can't go now. I can go in an hour.

chapters.guidedPractice: Transform 가다 into 가고 싶어요, 갈 수 있어요, 못 가요. Transform 먹다 into 먹고 싶어요, 먹을 수 있어요, 못 먹어요.
chapters.realLifeTask: Say one thing you want to do, one thing you can do, and one thing you cannot do today.
chapters.friendPractice: Friend asks 갈 수 있어요? Learner answers with 갈 수 있어요 or 못 가요 and a reason.
chapters.review: Can you explain why 못 가해요 is wrong and say 못 가요 instead?

beginnerGuide.title: Three different meanings
beginnerGuide.body: 고 싶어요 is desire, ㄹ/을 수 있어요 is ability or possibility, and 못 + verb is inability. They are not interchangeable.

beginnerGuide.title: The 못 rule beginners need
beginnerGuide.body: For most verbs, put 못 before the normal verb: 못 가요, 못 먹어요. For 하다 verbs, use 못 해요 or noun 못 해요: 공부 못 해요. Do not make 못 가해요.

beginnerGuide.title: Why this chapter matters
beginnerGuide.body: This is the chapter that lets you explain limits politely: I want to go, I can go, I cannot go, I cannot eat spicy food.

checkpoints: I can say V고 싶어요 for something I want.
I can say Vㄹ/을 수 있어요 for something possible.
I can use 못 for a real limitation, not just preference.

chapters.title: Requests, Permission, And Prohibition

chapters.scenario: A museum or store where the learner wants help and asks whether photos are okay.

dialogue.speaker: Learner

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.en: Sure, what can I help you with?

dialogue.speaker: Learner

dialogue.speaker: Staff

beginnerGuide.title: Requests and permission are different

beginnerGuide.title: Prohibition is mostly for understanding first
beginnerGuide.body: 지 마세요 appears on signs and from staff. You can use it, but it can sound like an instruction, so beginners should learn to understand it before using it broadly.

beginnerGuide.title: Make requests softer
beginnerGuide.body: 좀 often softens ordinary requests: 좀 도와주세요, 물 좀 주세요, 잠깐 기다려 주세요.

chapters.title: Travel And Classroom Help
chapters.goal: Ask for directions or repetition when you are lost or missed something.
chapters.scenario: A station or hotel lobby where the learner needs one clear answer.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Excuse me, where is the bathroom?

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.en: It's over there on the right.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.ko: 다시 한 번만 천천히 말해 주세요.
dialogue.romanization: dasi han beonman cheoncheonhi malhae juseyo.

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.en: Sure. It's over there on the right.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I understand. Thank you.

chapters.guidedPractice: Ask where something is, ask someone to repeat, and explain that you do not understand yet.

beginnerGuide.body: When communication breaks down, phrases like 다시 말해 주세요, 천천히 말해 주세요, and 잘 모르겠어요 keep the conversation alive.

beginnerGuide.title: Ask short, useful questions

beginnerGuide.title: Range and route

chapters.title: Connecting Ideas
chapters.goal: Connect two small ideas so your Korean sounds like a real short explanation.
chapters.scenario: Two friends changing plans because one person is busy.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Why can't you come today?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: I can't go because I have work.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Then if you have time, shall we meet tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Sounds good. I'll call after I finish.

chapters.guidedPractice: Combine two ideas with 아서/어서, then make one promise with ㄹ/을게요.
chapters.realLifeTask: Explain why you cannot do something today, then make one simple next plan.
chapters.friendPractice: Friend asks 왜요? Learner answers with one reason sentence.
chapters.review: Can you connect two simple ideas without making a long confusing sentence?

beginnerGuide.title: Longer Korean starts with connectors
beginnerGuide.body: 아서/어서, 고, and 면 let you connect simple sentences. This is how beginner Korean stops sounding like isolated flashcards.

beginnerGuide.title: Reason, sequence, condition
beginnerGuide.body: 아서/어서 gives a reason, 고 connects actions or descriptions, and 면 gives a condition. 바빠서 못 가요, 먹고 가요, 시간이 있으면 전화해 주세요.

beginnerGuide.title: Promise form
beginnerGuide.body: ㄹ/을게요 is for the speaker’s decision or promise: 제가 할게요, 기다릴게요, 전화할게요. Do not use it to predict someone else.

checkpoints: I can connect a reason with 아서/어서.
I can make a simple condition with 면.
I can promise the next action with ㄹ/을게요.

chapters.title: Past Tense
chapters.goal: Answer what you did yesterday with one clean past-tense sentence.
chapters.scenario: A friend asks about yesterday's evening, weekend, or class.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Yesterday I watched a movie with a friend.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: How was it?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: It was fun. But the weather was a bit cold.

beginnerGuide.body: When you see 어제, 지난주, or 작년, check that the verb ending is past tense too.

beginnerGuide.title: Memorize the shortcuts
beginnerGuide.body: The forms 했어요, 봤어요, 왔어요, and 갔어요 appear constantly. Learn them as whole spoken chunks.

naturalWhy.title: Why past tense sounds natural here
naturalWhy.todayScene: Someone asks 어제 뭐 했어요? The time word 어제 already tells the listener the event is finished.
naturalWhy.why: 어제 points to a finished time, so Korean expects the verb ending to match that finished feeling. 봐요 sounds like now, usually, or a future plan. 봤어요 closes the event and matches 어제.
koreanSense: 오늘 봐요 feels present or scheduled.
어제 봤어요 feels finished and easy to understand.
내일 볼 거예요 points forward, so it should not use past tense.

chapters.title: Future and Intention
chapters.goal: Say a real future plan, not just a grammar example.
chapters.scenario: You are making a weekend or evening plan with someone.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: What are you going to do this weekend?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: I am going to meet a friend and go to a cafe.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: What if it rains?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: If it rains, I am going to study at home.

chapters.guidedPractice: Write five future-plan sentences with 내일, 이번 주말, or 방학. Include both a vowel-stem form like 갈 거예요 and a consonant-stem form like 먹을 거예요.
chapters.realLifeTask: Answer 주말에 뭐 할 거예요? and add what you will do if the plan changes.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner gives you a situation; answer with one sentence that uses the chapter's main pattern or vocabulary.
chapters.review: Can you explain why 비가 올게요 is wrong and 비가 올 거예요 is right?

beginnerGuide.title: Separate plan and promise
beginnerGuide.body: -(으)ㄹ 거예요 states a plan or prediction. -(으)ㄹ게요 is a promise or offer to the listener.

beginnerGuide.title: Check the stem ending
beginnerGuide.body: Vowel stems take ㄹ 거예요: 갈 거예요, 볼 거예요, 할 거예요. Consonant stems take 을 거예요: 먹을 거예요, 읽을 거예요.

beginnerGuide.title: Use real time words
beginnerGuide.body: Practice with 내일, 이번 주말, 오늘 밤, and 방학 so the future frame is tied to real plans.

checkpoints: I can use -(으)ㄹ 거예요 for a plan or prediction.
I can use -면 for a simple condition.
I can tell apart 할 거예요 from 할게요.

chapters.title: Question Words
chapters.goal: Ask better follow-up questions so the conversation does not stop.
chapters.scenario: You are getting to know a classmate, tutor, or language partner.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Where do you learn Korean?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: I learn at home through an online class.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: When did you start?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: I started last year.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Why do you study Korean?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 한국 친구들과 더 편하게 이야기하고 싶어서요.
dialogue.romanization: hanguk chingudeulgwa deo pyeonhage iyagihago sipeoseoyo.
dialogue.en: Because I want to talk more comfortably with Korean friends.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: How do you usually practice?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: I watch dramas and repeat the sentences.

chapters.guidedPractice: Write one question each with 뭐, 어디, 언제, 왜, 어떻게, 누구, then answer three of them in Korean.
chapters.realLifeTask: Ask three follow-up questions using 어디, 언제, 왜, 어떻게, or 누구.
chapters.friendPractice: Partner says 한국어를 배워요. Ask three follow-up questions using different question words, then listen for the answer slot.
chapters.review: Can you explain the difference between 어디에 가요? and 어디에서 공부해요?

beginnerGuide.title: Question words replace answers
beginnerGuide.body: Think from the answer first. 학교에서 공부해요 becomes 어디에서 공부해요? 친구를 만나요 becomes 누구를 만나요?

beginnerGuide.title: Particles still matter
beginnerGuide.body: Use 어디에 for destination or location, 어디에서 for the place where an action happens, 누구를 for the person you meet, and 누구랑 for the person you do something with.

beginnerGuide.title: Do not mix up 어떻게 and 어때요
beginnerGuide.body: 어떻게 asks how to do something: 어떻게 가요? 어때요 asks for an opinion or condition: 영화 어때요?

checkpoints: I can pick the question word that matches the missing answer.
I can keep the question word in the Korean answer slot.
I can ask a short follow-up like 왜요? or 언제부터요?

beginnerGuide.title: The unit chooses the number family
beginnerGuide.body: Hours and common counters use native numbers: 한 시, 두 잔, 세 명. Minutes, dates, and prices use Sino-Korean numbers: 십 분, 이월 삼일, 오천 원.

beginnerGuide.title: Native numbers change before counters
beginnerGuide.body: 하나, 둘, 셋, 넷 become 한, 두, 세, 네 before counters: 한 시, 두 잔, 세 명, 네 개.

beginnerGuide.title: Age needs politeness
beginnerGuide.body: 나이가 어떻게 되세요? is a safer polite question than 몇 살이에요? with adults or people you do not know well.

I can use Sino-Korean numbers for minutes, dates, and prices.
I can avoid mixing 세 시 and 삼 분 the wrong way.

beginnerGuide.title: Change before vowel endings

beginnerGuide.title: Learn useful pairs

beginnerGuide.title: Hangul is regular, speech is connected
beginnerGuide.body: Korean spelling is reliable, but spoken Korean connects blocks: 먹어요 is read closer to [머거요], and 한국어 is read closer to [한구거].

beginnerGuide.title: Blocked sounds can push the next sound
beginnerGuide.body: After a final consonant, the next plain sound can become tense: 학교 [학꾜], 국밥 [국빱], 먹고 [먹꼬].

beginnerGuide.title: Nasals and ㅎ change neighbors

dialogue.speaker: A

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: It was fun. But the weather was a bit cold.

beginnerGuide.title: Timeline words

I can use -자마자 for immediately after.
I can use -기 전에 for before doing something.

chapters.goal: Explain when an action changed, got interrupted, or ended in a new state.
chapters.scenario: You started one plan, but something happened while you were doing it.

dialogue.ko: 학교에 가다가 수업 취소 문자를 받았어요.
dialogue.romanization: hakgyoe gadaga sueop chwiso munjareul badasseoyo.
dialogue.en: I got a class cancellation text while I was on my way to school.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 지하철을 타고 있다가 수업 취소 문자를 받았어요?
dialogue.romanization: jihacheoreul tago itdaga sueop chwiso munjareul badasseoyo?

beginnerGuide.title: Interrupted action
beginnerGuide.body: Use -다가 when the first action is underway and then something changes: 학교에 가다가 전화를 받았어요.

beginnerGuide.title: Changed plan words
beginnerGuide.body: 중간에, 계획, 바꾸다, 취소하다, 문자, and 갑자기 help explain why the original action changed.

beginnerGuide.title: Result state
beginnerGuide.body: Use -아/어 있어요 for the state that remains: 앉아 있어요, 문이 열려 있어요, 불이 켜져 있어요.

I can use -아/어 있다 for a state that remains after an action.
I can keep the before-and-after order clear.

chapters.goal: Explain a cause and an unexpected result naturally.
chapters.scenario: Weather, traffic, mistakes, or sudden plans changed what happened.

chapters.guidedPractice: Make one sentence with each cause shape: 길이 막혀서 늦었어요, 버스가 고장 나는 바람에 늦었어요, 비 때문에 취소했어요. Then change the cause word.
chapters.realLifeTask: Say one thing that happened because of a problem using -아서/어서 or -는 바람에.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner asks 왜 늦었어요? or 왜 취소됐어요? Answer once with -아서/어서, once with -는 바람에, and once with N 때문에.
chapters.review: Can you choose between neutral cause, unexpected-disruption cause, and noun cause without saying 비가 때문에?

beginnerGuide.title: Three cause shapes
beginnerGuide.body: Use -아서/어서 for ordinary reason-result, -는 바람에 for an unexpected event that caused trouble, and N 때문에 when the cause is a noun.

beginnerGuide.title: Use real situation words
beginnerGuide.body: 비, 길, 버스, 택시, 약속, 모임, 막히다, 고장나다, 놓치다, 늦다, and 취소하다 all belong to the same late-or-canceled-plan scene.

beginnerGuide.title: Watch the tone
beginnerGuide.body: 바람에 can sound like an excuse because it points to something that disrupted the plan. If someone waited for you, add 죄송해요 or 미안해요.

checkpoints: I can use -아서/어서 for ordinary cause and result.
I can use -는 바람에 for an unwanted or unexpected result.
I can avoid using -아서/어서 with commands or suggestions.

chapters.title: Purpose and Duration
chapters.goal: Talk about purpose and time span in one clear plan.
chapters.scenario: You study for a test, save money for a trip, or work from one time to another.

dialogue.en: What are you going to do this weekend?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: I am going to meet a friend and go to a cafe.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: What if it rains?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: If it rains, I am going to study at home.

chapters.guidedPractice: Make two purpose sentences and two duration sentences: 배우기 위해서 왔어요, 취업을 위해서 연습해요, 세 달 동안 머물 거예요, 한국에 있는 동안 공부할 거예요.
chapters.realLifeTask: Say what you are doing for a purpose and from when to when.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner asks 왜 왔어요? and 얼마 동안 있을 거예요? Answer with -기 위해서, N을/를 위해서, N 동안, and V-는 동안.
chapters.review: Can you keep purpose 'for' and duration 'for' separate in Korean?

beginnerGuide.title: Two kinds of for
beginnerGuide.body: English uses 'for' in 취업을 위해서 and 세 달 동안, but Korean separates purpose from duration. 위해서 gives the goal; 동안 gives the time span.

beginnerGuide.title: Purpose needs the right shape
beginnerGuide.body: Use V-기 위해서 for verb goals like 배우기 위해서 and 합격하기 위해서. Use N을/를 위해서 for noun goals like 취업을 위해서 and 건강을 위해서.

beginnerGuide.title: Duration is a span
beginnerGuide.body: Use 세 달 동안, 방학 동안, and 한국에 있는 동안 to show the time period. Do not say 세 달에 동안 or 방학에 동안.

checkpoints: I can use -기 위해서 for purpose.
I can use 전에 and 후에 around events.
I can use 부터 and 까지 for a time or place range.

chapters.goal: Say 'but' and 'even though' with the right amount of contrast.

chapters.guidedPractice: Make three pairs: 비싸지만 맛있어요, 비싸도 갈 거예요, 비싼데도 사람이 많아요. Say what changes in the feeling each time.
chapters.realLifeTask: Describe one mixed situation using -지만, 그런데, or -아/어도.
chapters.friendPractice: One person gives an obstacle such as 비싸요, 어려워요, 피곤해요. The other answers with -지만, -아/어도, or -는데도 and explains the choice.
chapters.review: Can you separate simple contrast (-지만), condition that does not change the result (-아/어도), and surprising result (-는데도)?

beginnerGuide.title: Three kinds of but
beginnerGuide.body: -지만 is the plain contrast form: 비싸지만 맛있어요. Use it when two facts pull in different directions without extra emotion.

beginnerGuide.title: Even if the plan stays
beginnerGuide.body: -아/어도 says the result does not change: 비가 와도 갈 거예요, 어려워도 해 볼게요. 괜찮아요 and 상관없어요 pair naturally with this form.

beginnerGuide.title: Even though it is surprising
beginnerGuide.body: -는데도 reacts to an actual situation where the expected result did not happen: 비가 오는데도 사람이 많아요. It sounds stronger than plain -지만.

checkpoints: I can use -지만 inside one sentence.
I can use 그런데 when the next sentence changes direction.
I can use -아/어도 when the problem does not stop the result.

beginnerGuide.body: Use -(으)ㄹ 것 같아요 when you have an impression but not a fact: 비가 올 것 같아요, 조금 늦을 것 같아요.

beginnerGuide.title: Agency comes first
beginnerGuide.body: Use -기로 했어요 when you made the decision. Use -게 됐어요 when circumstances led to the result. Use -아/어졌어요 when the state itself changed.

beginnerGuide.title: Use change words together
beginnerGuide.body: 결정하다, 시작하다, 바뀌다, 달라지다, 좋아지다, 늘다, and 줄다 help explain what changed in a real routine or study plan.

beginnerGuide.title: Do not hide decisions
beginnerGuide.body: If you simply chose something, say 운동하기로 했어요. Use 운동하게 됐어요 only when the situation led you there.

naturalWhy.title: Why past tense sounds natural here
naturalWhy.todayScene: Someone asks 어제 뭐 했어요? The time word 어제 already tells the listener the event is finished.
naturalWhy.why: 어제 points to a finished time, so Korean expects the verb ending to match that finished feeling. 봐요 sounds like now, usually, or a future plan. 봤어요 closes the event and matches 어제.
koreanSense: 오늘 봐요 feels present or scheduled.
어제 봤어요 feels finished and easy to understand.
내일 볼 거예요 points forward, so it should not use past tense.

dialogue.speaker: B

chapters.guidedPractice: Rewrite the same noun with three particles: 친구에게, 친구랑, 친구도; then contrast 공부만 해요 with 공부밖에 못 해요.
chapters.realLifeTask: Write one sentence with 에게/한테 and one with 도 or 만.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner gives a noun like 친구, 선생님, 커피, 시간, or 공부; answer with a sentence using 도, 만, 밖에, 이라도, or 에게/께.
chapters.review: Can you choose the right particle for also, only, receiver, possession, with, as many as, and at least without mixing their jobs?

beginnerGuide.title: Particles change the job
beginnerGuide.body: 친구 can become 친구에게 (to a friend), 친구랑 (with a friend), 친구도 (a friend too), 친구만 (only a friend), or 친구의 (a friend's). The noun is the same; the relationship changes.

beginnerGuide.title: 만 and 밖에 are not twins
beginnerGuide.body: 공부만 해요 is neutral: I only study. 공부밖에 못 해요 needs a negative predicate and feels limited: I can do nothing but study.

beginnerGuide.title: 이라도 gives a minimum option
beginnerGuide.body: 커피라도 마실래요? means coffee is not the full plan, but it is at least something possible. It is different from 커피만 and 커피도.

checkpoints: I can use 에게/한테 for a person receiving something.
I can use 도 for also and 만 for only.
I can use 의 carefully for possession or noun-to-noun links.

chapters.guidedPractice: Choose one role noun and one time noun, then make five sentences: past identity, background, reason with 라서, reason with 니까, and a fallback with 라도.

chapters.friendPractice: A partner asks about your role or schedule; answer with 학생이었어요, 회사원인데요, 주말이라서, 주말이니까, or 한 시간이라도.
chapters.review: Can you explain why 학생, 회사원, 주말, 평일, 아침, and 시간 fit this chapter better than random nouns?

beginnerGuide.title: 이다 changes nouns into sentence material
beginnerGuide.body: This chapter should start from nouns that naturally become identity or schedule explanations: 학생이었어요, 회사원인데요, 주말이라서, 평일이니까.

beginnerGuide.title: 라서 explains; 니까 often leads to action
beginnerGuide.body: 회사원이라서 한국어가 필요해요 simply explains the cause. 주말이니까 공부해요 sounds more like a reason for a decision or suggestion.

beginnerGuide.title: 라도 is the fallback marker
beginnerGuide.body: 한 시간이라도 공부해요 means one hour is not ideal, but it is still worth doing. That is why 시간 is a useful core noun here.

checkpoints: I can use 이에요/예요 after nouns.
I can use 이라서/라서 for because it is a noun.
I can use 이면/면 and 이고/고 with noun predicates.

beginnerGuide.title: Count people with 명, not 개
beginnerGuide.body: 가족이 몇 명이에요? and 저희 가족은 네 명이에요 are the base sentences. People take 명, and the number before 명 is native Korean: 한, 두, 세, 네, 다섯.

beginnerGuide.title: Sibling terms depend on the speaker
beginnerGuide.body: A male speaker says 형 for an older brother and 누나 for an older sister. A female speaker says 오빠 and 언니. 동생 works for a younger sibling.

beginnerGuide.title: Honor the subject with 께서 and -(으)시-
beginnerGuide.body: 부모님께서 오세요 and 어머니께서 오셨어요 honor the person doing the action. 께서 is for the subject; 께 without 서 marks a respected receiver.

beginnerGuide.title: Setting changes the ending
beginnerGuide.body: Use 합쇼체 in formal public settings like 발표 and 면접. Use 해요체 for ordinary polite conversation with classmates, teachers, and people you just met.

beginnerGuide.title: Polite is not one style
beginnerGuide.body: 존댓말 is the broad polite category. 해요체 and 합쇼체 are both polite, but 합쇼체 sounds more formal and public.

beginnerGuide.title: Use 반말 carefully
beginnerGuide.body: 반말 is natural with close friends, but it can sound rude with teachers, staff, strangers, or people who have not agreed to speak casually.

beginnerGuide.title: Respect has direction
beginnerGuide.body: -(으)시- and 께서 honor the subject. 께 and 드리다 honor the person who receives your action.

beginnerGuide.title: Use special verbs
beginnerGuide.body: 계시다, 드시다, 주무시다, and 말씀하시다 are not random alternatives; they are common honorific verbs for respected subjects.

beginnerGuide.title: Do not honor yourself

chapters.goal: Bring up background information without sounding abrupt.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 그러니까 먼저 회의를 시작해도 된다는 말이죠?
dialogue.romanization: geureonikka meonjeo hoeuireul sijakaedo doendaneun marijyo?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Yes. Something suddenly came up yesterday, you see.

dialogue.speaker: B

dialogue.romanization: algesseoyo. geureonde balpyo jeone jaryoneun bonae jul su isseoyo?

dialogue.speaker: A

dialogue.romanization: ne, geugeon ganeunghaeyo. hoeui sigani jjaljanhayo.

dialogue.speaker: B

beginnerGuide.title: Open the topic softly
beginnerGuide.body: 사실은 and -는데요 let you start a sensitive topic without sounding like you are dropping bad news too suddenly.

beginnerGuide.title: Separate new and shared information
beginnerGuide.body: Use -거든요 when the listener does not know the background yet. Use -잖아요 when the listener already knows or can see the reason.

beginnerGuide.title: Soften disagreement
beginnerGuide.body: 그런데, 근데, and -는데요 can make pushback feel conversational, but the sentence still needs a clear point.

I can use -거든요 for new background the listener may not know.
I can use -잖아요 only when the listener likely knows or agrees.

chapters.goal: Navigate Korean social habits without sounding rude or too casual.

dialogue.ko: 집들이에 갈 때 휴지랑 세제 중에 뭐가 나아요?
dialogue.romanization: jipdeurie gal ttae hyujirang seje junge mwoga naayo?
dialogue.en: When going to a housewarming, which is better, toilet paper or detergent?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 둘 다 괜찮아요. 집들이 선물로 많이 가져가잖아요.
dialogue.romanization: dul da gwaenchanayo. jipdeuri seonmullo manhi gajyeogajanhayo.
dialogue.en: Both are fine. People often bring them as housewarming gifts, you know.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: If we are about the same age, can I say we are the same age?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 그래도 처음엔 선배님 같은 호칭을 쓰는 편이에요.
dialogue.romanization: geuraedo cheoeumen seonbaenim gateun hochingeul sseuneun pyeonieyo.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: If elders are there too, I will ask, 'May I help?'

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 좋아요. 눈치 있게 챙기면 분위기가 덜 어색해요.
dialogue.romanization: joayo. nunchi itge chaenggimyeon bunwigiga deol eosaekaeyo.

naturalWhy.title: Why past tense sounds natural here
naturalWhy.todayScene: Someone asks 어제 뭐 했어요? The time word 어제 already tells the listener the event is finished.
naturalWhy.why: 어제 points to a finished time, so Korean expects the verb ending to match that finished feeling. 봐요 sounds like now, usually, or a future plan. 봤어요 closes the event and matches 어제.
koreanSense: 오늘 봐요 feels present or scheduled.
어제 봤어요 feels finished and easy to understand.
내일 볼 거예요 points forward, so it should not use past tense.

beginnerGuide.title: Clinic and pharmacy words belong together

beginnerGuide.title: Firsthand evidence

beginnerGuide.title: Observed change
beginnerGuide.body: -더니 links an earlier thing you observed to the change or result that followed: 처음에는 조용하더니 금방 붐볐어요.

beginnerGuide.title: Your own result

dialogue.speaker: A

beginnerGuide.title: Forecast language changes plans
beginnerGuide.body: 일기예보를 보고 비가 올 것 같아요, 태풍이 올 텐데요, 미세먼지 때문에 취소해요처럼 계획을 조정해요.

beginnerGuide.title: 미세먼지 is plan vocabulary

chapters.guidedPractice: Turn three blunt statements into careful Korean: one with -ㄹ걸요, one with -다면, and one with -는 것 같아요.
chapters.realLifeTask: Make one soft guess and one small regret.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner gives you an uncertain workplace or group-chat situation; answer with a guess, a hypothetical, and a gentle suggestion.
chapters.review: Can you choose between -ㄹ걸요, -다면, -겠-, 좋겠어요, and 것 같아요 instead of using one vague 'I think' for everything?

beginnerGuide.title: Guess without overclaiming
beginnerGuide.body: -ㄹ걸요 gives a soft but fairly confident guess: 아직 회의 중일걸요. Use it when you have a hunch, not when you are simply unsure.

beginnerGuide.title: Open a careful possibility
beginnerGuide.body: -다면 sets up a what-if frame: 이미 나갔다면. It lets you discuss the next step without pretending you know the fact.

beginnerGuide.title: Soften the opinion itself
beginnerGuide.body: 것 같아요 softens a whole impression or opinion. Do not treat it as 같다 meaning 'same'; here it means 'it seems / I think.'

I can use -ㄹ걸요 for a careful prediction.

beginnerGuide.title: Check particles
beginnerGuide.body: Use 에서 for the transfer place, 으로/로 for the line or means, 때문에 for the delay cause, and 때 for the moment you book or transfer.

beginnerGuide.title: Find the final noun
beginnerGuide.body: In long Korean noun phrases, the important noun comes at the end: 올라온 공지, 변경된 일정, 제출할 보고서.

beginnerGuide.title: Passive focuses the result

naturalWhy.title: Why past tense sounds natural here
naturalWhy.todayScene: Someone asks 어제 뭐 했어요? The time word 어제 already tells the listener the event is finished.
naturalWhy.why: 어제 points to a finished time, so Korean expects the verb ending to match that finished feeling. 봐요 sounds like now, usually, or a future plan. 봤어요 closes the event and matches 어제.
koreanSense: 오늘 봐요 feels present or scheduled.
어제 봤어요 feels finished and easy to understand.
내일 볼 거예요 points forward, so it should not use past tense.

chapters.title: Topic vs Subject — 은/는 and 이/가
chapters.goal: Choose 은/는 or 이/가 based on what the listener needs to notice.
chapters.scenario: You introduce new information, continue a topic, or contrast two people or things.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: A friend called.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Does that friend call often?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 아니요. 평소에는 메시지를 보내는데 오늘은 제가 먼저 연락했어요.
dialogue.romanization: aniyo. pyeongsoeneun mesijireul bonaeneunde oneureun jega meonjeo yeollakaesseoyo.
dialogue.en: No. Usually they send messages, but today I contacted them first.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Who contacted them first?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 제가 먼저 연락했어요. 질문은 쉬웠는데 대답이 어려웠어요.
dialogue.romanization: jega meonjeo yeollakaesseoyo. jilmuneun swiwonneunde daedabi eoryeowosseoyo.
dialogue.en: I contacted them first. The question was easy, but the answer was difficult.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 그럼 이 문제는 이유가 제일 중요하네요.
dialogue.romanization: geureom i munjeneun iyuga jeil jungyohaneyo.
dialogue.en: Then for this issue, the reason is the most important thing.

chapters.guidedPractice: Write one sentence that introduces new information with 이/가, one that continues a topic with 은/는, one contrast sentence, and one topic-plus-subject sentence.
chapters.realLifeTask: Describe one real message or event using both 은/는 and 이/가.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner asks 누가?, 무엇이?, or 그 사람은? Answer with 이/가 for focused answers and 은/는 for topic or contrast.
chapters.review: Can you explain why 친구가 전화했어요, 그 친구는 자주 전화해요, and 제가 먼저 연락했어요 use different particles?

beginnerGuide.title: New or focused information
beginnerGuide.body: Use 이/가 when the sentence answers who or what, introduces a subject, or points to exactly one answer: 친구가 전화했어요, 제가 먼저 했어요.

beginnerGuide.title: Topic and contrast
beginnerGuide.body: Use 은/는 when the noun is already the topic or when you are contrasting: 그 친구는..., 메시지는 보내지만 전화는 안 해요.

beginnerGuide.title: Frame plus new subject
beginnerGuide.body: Korean can use both in one sentence: 이 문제는 이유가 중요해요. The topic is the frame; 이/가 introduces the important subject inside that frame.

checkpoints: I can use 이/가 for new or focused information.
I can use 은/는 for topic, contrast, or continuation.
I can build sentences like 이 문제는 이유가 중요해요.

chapters.title: 겠 — Volition, Inference, and Softened Speech
chapters.goal: Use 겠 for formal intention, careful guessing, or polite softening.
chapters.scenario: You promise to handle something, infer a result, or politely decline.

dialogue.speaker: Customer
dialogue.en: Could you check my order, please?

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.en: Yes, I will check it right away.

dialogue.speaker: Customer
dialogue.en: There are many people, so it looks like it will take some time.

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.en: Yes, it will take about ten minutes.

dialogue.speaker: Customer
dialogue.en: Then I will wait here.

dialogue.speaker: Staff

chapters.guidedPractice: Write two service commitments with -겠습니다, two evidence-based inferences with -겠네요, and one softened refusal with 어렵겠습니다.
chapters.realLifeTask: Make one sentence with -겠습니다 and one guess with -겠네요.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner gives a context: service promise, inference, future plan, or soft refusal. Choose 겠, -(으)ㄹ 거예요, or -(으)ㄹ 것 같아요.

beginnerGuide.title: Separate three jobs
beginnerGuide.body: 겠 can mark a formal commitment, a confident inference, or softened formal speech. Do not translate every 겠 as simple future.

beginnerGuide.title: Service promise
beginnerGuide.body: In service or workplace speech, 확인하겠습니다 and 처리하겠습니다 sound like committed action. 확인할 거예요 sounds more like a plain future plan.

beginnerGuide.title: Inference and refusal
beginnerGuide.body: 피곤하시겠네요 infers from evidence. 참석하기 어렵겠습니다 softens a refusal instead of bluntly saying 못 가요.

chapters.goal: Add the speaker's reaction at the end of the sentence.
chapters.scenario: You notice something, feel surprise, make a careful prediction, or express regret.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Korean is more fun than I expected.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 처음에는 어려울 줄 알았는데 생각보다 괜찮군요.
dialogue.romanization: cheoeumeneun eoryeoul jul aranneunde saenggakboda gwaenchanhgunyo.
dialogue.en: I thought it would be hard at first, but it is better than expected.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Oh, they have already arrived.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: If you leave now, you will probably be a little late.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 어제 시간이 있었으면 같이 갔을 텐데요.
dialogue.romanization: eoje sigani isseosseumyeon gachi gasseul tendeyo.
dialogue.en: If I had had time yesterday, I would have gone with you.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 연습을 많이 했으니까 잘하는 게 당연하네요.
dialogue.romanization: yeonseubeul mani haesseunikka jalhaneun ge dangyeonhaneyo.
dialogue.en: Since you practiced a lot, no wonder you are good.

chapters.guidedPractice: Write one fresh realization with -네요, one formal realization with -군요, one hedged prediction with -ㄹ걸요, and one regret with -았/었을 텐데요.
chapters.realLifeTask: React to one real situation with -네요, -군요, -ㄹ걸요, or -았/었을 텐데요.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner gives you a fact or situation. Choose whether your response should sound like fresh noticing, formal acknowledgement, hedged prediction, or regret.
chapters.review: Can you explain why 재미있네요, 도착하셨군요, 늦을걸요, and 갔을 텐데요 do not have the same speaker attitude?

beginnerGuide.title: Read the speaker's attitude
beginnerGuide.body: These endings do not just add politeness. They tell the listener whether you just noticed something, are acknowledging new information, are guessing, or are regretting a missed outcome.

beginnerGuide.title: Separate noticing from knowing
beginnerGuide.body: -네요 works when the speaker is freshly realizing something. If you already knew it, a plain statement or -잖아요 may fit better.

beginnerGuide.title: Keep regret and prediction apart
beginnerGuide.body: -ㄹ걸요 can hedge a prediction, while -았/었을 텐데요 looks back at a missed past condition. Do not flatten both into English would/probably.

I can use -군요 for a stronger or more formal realization.

beginnerGuide.title: Use -기 for activity labels
beginnerGuide.body: 운동하기, 공부하기, 걷기 can name an activity as a task, goal, or habit plan. This form is common before 어렵다, 쉽다, 전에, 위해, 시작하다, and 기로 했어요.

beginnerGuide.title: Use -는 것 for a concrete action
beginnerGuide.body: 친구가 걷는 것을 봤어요 and 매일 늦게 먹는 것을 줄이고 있어요 point to an action you see, know, feel, or treat as a concrete habit.

sampleAnswer.en: Listening every day is hard. Still, repeating sentences helps.

I can use -는 것/거 for a specific action, fact, or event.
I can keep fixed expressions like -기로 했어요 and -기 전에.

chapters.title: Causative Verbs
chapters.goal: Say who makes, lets, or has someone do something.
chapters.scenario: A parent feeds a child, a teacher has students read, or a manager seats guests.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Did you look after your niece or nephew today?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Yes. I fed them and put them down for a nap too.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: When you went outside, did you put a coat on them too?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Yes, I did. The toy made the child laugh.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 이렇게 보면 누가 누구에게 무엇을 하게 했는지가 보이네요.
dialogue.romanization: ireoke bomyeon nuga nuguege mueoseul hage haenneunjiga boineyo.
dialogue.en: Seen this way, you can tell who made someone do what.

chapters.guidedPractice: Write five pairs: base action first, causative action second. Example: 아이가 먹어요 -> 엄마가 아이에게 밥을 먹여요.
chapters.realLifeTask: Describe one scene with a causative verb, then rewrite it with -게 하다.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner gives a base verb; answer with a natural causative pair and one full sentence.
chapters.review: Can you tell who does the action and who causes it in 먹다/먹이다, 자다/재우다, 앉다/앉히다, 웃다/웃기다, and 울다/울리다?

beginnerGuide.title: Find the causer
beginnerGuide.body: In 사동 sentences, the subject is often not doing the base action. 엄마가 아이에게 밥을 먹였어요 means the child eats, but the mother causes or helps it happen.

beginnerGuide.title: Learn pairs, not suffix math
beginnerGuide.body: The suffix list is useful, but many causatives are memorized as pairs: 먹다/먹이다, 자다/재우다, 입다/입히다, 앉다/앉히다, 울다/울리다.

beginnerGuide.title: Separate causative and passive
beginnerGuide.body: Some forms look like passive forms, especially 읽히다. Read the whole sentence: 선생님이 학생들에게 본문을 읽혔어요 is causative; 책이 잘 읽혀요 is text-focused/passive-like.

checkpoints: I can find the person causing the action and the person doing it.
I can use common causatives like 먹이다, 입히다, 앉히다, 웃기다, and 울리다.
I can compare a built-in causative with V-게 하다.

chapters.title: Unreal Conditionals
chapters.goal: Talk about a past choice that could have gone differently.
chapters.scenario: You missed a bus, found out too late, or wish you had said something earlier.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: I heard you were late for the interview yesterday?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 네. 버스를 놓치지 않았더라면 늦지 않았을 텐데요.
dialogue.romanization: ne. beoseureul nochiji anatdeoramyeon neutji anasseul tende-yo.
dialogue.en: Yes. If I had not missed the bus, I would not have been late.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: If you had known in advance, would you have taken a taxi?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 네. 조금만 일찍 나왔으면 좋았을 텐데요.
dialogue.romanization: ne. jogeumman iljjik nawasseumyeon joasseul tende-yo.
dialogue.en: Yes. It would have been nice if I had left just a little earlier.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 다음엔 전날에 길을 확인해 두면 좋겠어요.
dialogue.romanization: daeumen jeonnare gireul hwaginhae dumyeon jokesseoyo.
dialogue.en: Next time, it would be good to check the route the day before.

chapters.guidedPractice: Write one regret about information you did not know, one missed-transport situation, and one relationship regret using -았/었으면 or -았/었더라면.
chapters.realLifeTask: Turn one real regret into an unreal conditional sentence.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner gives a missed condition. Answer with the missed condition first, then a hypothetical result: -았/었더라면 ... -았/었을 거예요.
chapters.review: Can you make both halves hypothetical, instead of mixing a past condition with a plain real result?

beginnerGuide.title: Start from the missed condition
beginnerGuide.body: These sentences begin from something that did not happen: 미리 알다, 일찍 도착하다, 버스를 놓치지 않다, 바로 사과하다.

beginnerGuide.title: Make the result unreal too
beginnerGuide.body: After -았/었으면 or -았/었더라면, the second half usually needs -았/었을 텐데, -았/었을 거예요, or -았/었을지도 몰라요.

beginnerGuide.title: Use -더라면 for stronger hindsight
beginnerGuide.body: -았/었더라면 sounds more reflective and certain that the condition was missed. It fits regret, advice after the fact, and imagining a different outcome.

I can use -았/었더라면 for an unreal past condition.
I can pair the condition with -았/었을 텐데요 or -았/었을 거예요.

chapters.title: Korean Internet Language and Colloquial Intensifiers
chapters.goal: Read casual Korean online without carrying it into formal writing.
chapters.scenario: You read comments, KakaoTalk messages, live chat, or social posts.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 그 댓글 봤어? 완전 웃겨 ㅋㅋㅋ.
dialogue.romanization: geu daetgeul bwasseo? wanjeon utgyeo kkk.
dialogue.en: Did you see that comment? It's so funny lol.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Yeah, I saw it. Whoa, did you hit like?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 응, 친구한테 공유했어. 댓글 반응도 레전드야.
dialogue.romanization: eung, chinguhante gongyuhaesseo. daetgeul baneungdo rejeondeuya.
dialogue.en: Yeah, I shared it with a friend. The comment reactions are legendary too.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 공식 글에는 ㅋㅋ 빼고 재미있었습니다처럼 써야 해.
dialogue.romanization: gongsik geureneneun kk ppaego jaemiisseotseumnidacheoreom sseoya hae.
dialogue.en: In an official post, you should leave out ㅋㅋ and write something like 'it was interesting.'

chapters.guidedPractice: Rewrite five casual chat reactions for two settings: friend chat with ㅋㅋ/ㅇㅇ/완전, then official writing without slang.
chapters.realLifeTask: Sort three expressions into friend chat, polite chat, and formal writing.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner names a relationship: close friend, classmate, professor, company account, or livestream chat. Choose the reaction that fits the register.
chapters.review: Can you explain when ㅋㅋ, ㅠㅠ, ㅇㅇ, ㄹㅇ, ㅇㅈ, 대박, 완전, 레전드, and 개웃겨 are natural and when to replace them?

beginnerGuide.title: Register first
beginnerGuide.body: This chapter is about relationship and channel. ㅋㅋ and ㅇㅇ can be perfect in a friend chat and still be rude or careless in an email, professor message, or company notice.

beginnerGuide.title: Reaction families
beginnerGuide.body: Read the forms as families: ㅋㅋ/ㅠㅠ for emotion, ㅇㅇ/ㅇㅈ/ㄹㅇ for agreement or truth, and 완전/진짜/대박/레전드/개웃겨 for intensity.

beginnerGuide.title: Platform actions
beginnerGuide.body: Match digital nouns with their natural verbs: 댓글을 달다, 좋아요를 누르다, 친구한테 공유하다, 라이브 채팅에 올라오다.

I can use casual intensifiers like 완전, 진짜, 대박, and 레전드 with the right people.
I can remove internet markers from formal email or school writing.

chapters.title: Passive Verbs — 이/히/리/기, -아/어지다, and -게 되다
chapters.goal: Say what happened without naming who did it.
chapters.scenario: Your commute falls apart: the road is jammed, a call drops, and the meeting time changes.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 버스가 삼십 분째 안 와요. 무슨 일이죠?
dialogue.romanization: beoseuga samsip bunjjae an wayo. museun iljyo?
dialogue.en: The bus hasn't come for thirty minutes. What's going on?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 앞에 사고가 나서 도로가 꽉 막혔어요.
dialogue.romanization: ape sagoga naseo doroga kkwak makyeosseoyo.
dialogue.en: There was an accident up ahead, so the road is completely jammed.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Ah, that explains it. Shall we switch to the subway then?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 네. 근데 아까 전화가 끊겨서 팀장님께 아직 연락을 못 했어요.
dialogue.romanization: ne. geunde akka jeonhwaga kkeunkyeoseo timjangnimkke ajik yeollageul mot haesseoyo.
dialogue.en: Yes. But my call got cut off earlier, so I still haven't reached the team lead.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 지금 하세요. 회의 시간이 열 시로 바뀌었어요.
dialogue.romanization: jigeum haseyo. hoeui sigani yeol siro bakkwieosseoyo.
dialogue.en: Do it now. The meeting time was changed to ten.

chapters.guidedPractice: Take five things that went wrong today and say each one twice: once actively (누가 무엇을 했다) and once passively (무엇이 어떻게 됐다). Then decide which version a Korean colleague would actually say out loud.
chapters.realLifeTask: Send a three-sentence message reporting a delay without naming anyone, using 막히다, 끊기다, and 바뀌다.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner names a cause — 바람, 경찰, 시간, 강아지, 사고. You build a passive sentence and choose 에 or 에게/한테 correctly for each one.
chapters.review: Can you say 문이 닫혔어요 instead of 누가 문을 닫았어요, mark 바람에 and 경찰한테 correctly, and keep away from the double passive 열려졌어요?

beginnerGuide.title: Drop the doer first
beginnerGuide.body: Start from the active sentence, delete the person, and move the affected thing into the 이/가 slot: 직원이 문을 닫았어요 → 문이 닫혔어요. If 을/를 is still sitting in front of the passive verb, the sentence is not finished.

beginnerGuide.title: 에 or 에게 — is it alive?
beginnerGuide.body: Only a person or an animal takes 에게 or 한테. Wind, time, deadlines, accidents, and machines take plain 에. That single question fixes most of the passive mistakes English speakers make, because English uses one word, 'by', for all of them.

beginnerGuide.title: Three endings, three jobs
beginnerGuide.body: -이/히/리/기- is the built-in passive for a closed list of verbs. -아/어지다 covers the verbs that have no built-in form. -게 되다 is not a passive at all: it keeps the doer and only says circumstances made the decision. Never stack the first two — 열려졌어요 is a double passive.

checkpoints: I can rewrite an active sentence as a passive one and drop the object particle.
I can choose 에 or 에게/한테 for the cause without thinking about English 'by'.
I can tell 피동, 사동, and -게 되다 apart in a sentence I read.

chapters.title: Reported Speech, Contracted — -대요, -래요, -냬요, -재요
chapters.goal: Pass on what someone else said the way Koreans actually say it.
chapters.scenario: You are the middle of a group chat and a team notice: news, an instruction, a question, and an invitation all have to be relayed.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 무슨 공지 왔어요? 저는 못 봤는데요.
dialogue.romanization: museun gongji wasseoyo? jeoneun mot bwanneundeyo.
dialogue.en: What notice came through? I didn't see it.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: They say the team dinner got pushed to next week.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Ah, then what about the reservation?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 팀장님이 지훈 씨한테 다시 확인해 보래요.
dialogue.romanization: timjangnimi jihun ssihante dasi hwaginhae boraeyo.
dialogue.en: The team lead says to have Jihoon double-check it.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 알겠어요. 그리고 동기들이 그날 같이 가재요.
dialogue.romanization: algesseoyo. geurigo donggideuri geunal gachi gajaeyo.
dialogue.en: Got it. And the others say let's go together that day.

chapters.guidedPractice: Take four messages off your phone — a piece of news, an instruction, a question, and an invitation — and say each one out loud as if relaying it, naming who it came from.
chapters.realLifeTask: Relay four messages to a colleague using -대요, -래요, -냬요, and -재요, one of each.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner says a sentence in one of four shapes: a statement, an order, a question, or a suggestion. You repeat it back as if passing it on to somebody else.
chapters.review: Can you tell 학생이래요 from 가래요, and 갈래요 from 가래요, without stopping to think about it?

beginnerGuide.title: Only the tail gets shorter
beginnerGuide.body: The front of the sentence is exactly what it was with -다고 하다. A present-tense verb still needs its -ㄴ/는- (운동한대요), an adjective still attaches bare (바쁘대요), and any past still carries -았/었- (봤대요). Learn the four tails and the rest is already familiar.

beginnerGuide.title: There are two different 래요
beginnerGuide.body: After a noun, 래요 comes from -(이)라고 해요 and means 'they say it is': 학생이래요. After a verb stem it comes from -(으)라고 해요 and reports an order: 가래요. Look at the word in front to know which one you are hearing.

beginnerGuide.title: Name your source
beginnerGuide.body: A bare -래요 can sound as though you are giving the order yourself. Koreans almost always open with the person: 팀장님이 …래요, 엄마가 …래요. It makes clear you are the messenger, not the boss.

checkpoints: I can contract -다고 해요 to -대요 without losing the -ㄴ/는- on a verb.
I can choose between 학생이래요 and 가래요 by looking at the word in front.
I can relay a question with -냬요 and an invitation with -재요.

chapters.title: Reasons and Excuses — -느라고, -는 바람에, -더니, -았더니
chapters.goal: Say why something went wrong, and whose doing it was.
chapters.scenario: A Monday post-mortem: what you were too busy for, what hit you out of nowhere, and what you found out the hard way.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Why didn't you reply yesterday?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 짐 정리하느라고 휴대폰을 아예 못 봤어요.
dialogue.romanization: jim jeongnihaneurago hyudaeponeul aye mot bwasseoyo.
dialogue.en: I was sorting out my things, so I didn't look at my phone at all.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: And today? Why were you late this morning?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 지하철이 멈추는 바람에 삼십 분이나 서 있었어요.
dialogue.romanization: jihacheori meomchuneun barame samsip bunina seo isseosseoyo.
dialogue.en: The subway stopped, so I stood there for a full thirty minutes.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 고생했네요. 저는 어제 일찍 잤더니 오늘은 좀 괜찮아요.
dialogue.romanization: gosaenghaenneyo. jeoneun eoje iljjik jatdeoni oneureun jom gwaenchanayo.
dialogue.en: That sounds rough. I got to bed early yesterday, so I'm doing okay today.

chapters.guidedPractice: List three things that went wrong this week. For each one, decide whether you were the one who used up the time, whether something sudden hit you, or whether the result was actually fine — then pick -느라고, -는 바람에, or -아서/어서.
chapters.realLifeTask: Write four sentences about a bad Monday using -느라고, -는 바람에, -더니, and -았더니, one of each.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner names a cause and a result. You decide whether the two clauses share a subject, then choose the connector that fits.
chapters.review: Can you explain why 동생이 떠드는 바람에 제가 못 잤어요 works but 동생이 떠드느라고 제가 못 잤어요 does not?

beginnerGuide.title: Same subject or not
beginnerGuide.body: This one question sorts most of the chapter. -느라고 needs both halves to share a subject, because it means you personally were tied up in something. -는 바람에 does not, because it blames whatever hit you from outside. If the person who caused it is not the person who suffered it, you need -는 바람에.

beginnerGuide.title: The tense goes at the end
beginnerGuide.body: -느라고 and -는 바람에 never carry -았/었- themselves. 썼느라고 and 멈췄는 바람에 are both wrong. Put the past tense only in the final clause: 쓰느라고 못 잤어요, 멈추는 바람에 늦었어요.

beginnerGuide.title: Who was watching
beginnerGuide.body: -더니 reports something you watched somebody else do, so it does not sit with 제가. -았/었더니 reports your own past action and what you then discovered. 지훈 씨가 야근하더니 versus 제가 야근했더니.

checkpoints: I can keep one subject across both halves when I use -느라고.
I can leave the tense off -느라고 and -는 바람에 and put it in the final clause.
I can choose -더니 for somebody else and -았/었더니 for myself.

exitTask.prompt: Write four sentences about a bad Monday using -느라고, -는 바람에, -더니, and -았더니, one of each.

sampleAnswer.ko: 이사 준비하느라고 주말에 한숨도 못 잤어요. 오늘은 엘리베이터가 고장 나는 바람에 걸어 올라왔고요. 커피를 마셨더니 이제 좀 괜찮아요.
sampleAnswer.en: I was getting ready to move, so I didn't sleep a wink at the weekend. Today the lift broke down, so I walked up. I had a coffee, and now I'm doing a bit better.

chapters.title: Finished, Defeated, and Nearly — -아/어 버리다, -고 말다, -(으)ㄹ 뻔하다, -(으)ㄴ 척하다
chapters.goal: Say how something ended, and how you felt about the ending.
chapters.scenario: Looking back at one day: what you finished off, what beat you, what you barely avoided, and what you put a brave face on.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: How did that thing turn out yesterday?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: I stayed at it until late and got the whole thing done.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Nice work. But what's with your face?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 졸려서 계단에서 넘어질 뻔했어요. 괜찮은 척했는데 사실 놀랐어요.
dialogue.romanization: jollyeoseo gyedaneseo neomeojil ppeonhaesseoyo. gwaenchaneun cheokaenneunde sasil nollasseoyo.
dialogue.en: I was so sleepy I nearly fell on the stairs. I acted fine, but honestly it shook me.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 오늘은 일찍 들어가세요. 그러다 진짜 다치고 말 거예요.
dialogue.romanization: oneureun iljjik deureogaseyo. geureoda jinjja dachigo mal geoyeyo.
dialogue.en: Go home early today. At this rate you'll actually end up hurt.

chapters.guidedPractice: Take one thing you finished yesterday and say it twice: once with -아/어 버리다 and once with -고 말다. Notice that only one of the two can sit next to 후련해요.
chapters.realLifeTask: Write four sentences about yesterday using -아/어 버리다, -고 말다, 하마터면 …-(으)ㄹ 뻔했어요, and -(으)ㄴ/는 척하다.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner describes an ending and how it felt. You decide whether it takes -아/어 버리다 or -고 말다, and say why.
chapters.review: Can you explain why 기분 좋게 끝내 버렸어요 works but 기분 좋게 끝내고 말았어요 does not?

beginnerGuide.title: Did you want it to end that way?
beginnerGuide.body: -아/어 버리다 usually reports something you chose, and it can feel like relief: 다 끝내 버렸어요. -고 말다 reports an ending that beat you, and it never feels like relief: 결국 울고 말았어요. Ask how you felt about the ending before you pick one.

beginnerGuide.title: A near miss is always in the past
beginnerGuide.body: -(으)ㄹ 뻔했다 means it came close and then did not happen, so it lives in the past: 넘어질 뻔했어요. 하마터면 is its usual partner at the front. Watch out for standalone 뻔하다 — that is a different word meaning 'obvious'.

beginnerGuide.title: Check the base word before 척하다
beginnerGuide.body: Verbs in progress take -는 척하다 (자는 척), finished actions take -(으)ㄴ 척하다 (못 들은 척), and adjectives also take -(으)ㄴ (아픈 척). 아프는 척하다 is the mistake almost every English speaker makes at least once.

checkpoints: I can choose -아/어 버리다 or -고 말다 based on how the ending felt.
I can keep -(으)ㄹ 뻔했다 in the past and pair it with 하마터면.
I can pick -는 or -(으)ㄴ in front of 척하다 by checking the base word.

chapters.title: Advanced Written Korean
chapters.goal: Make formal writing easier to follow with clear connectors.
chapters.scenario: You write a short report, complaint, summary, or project update.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: This report lacks evidence.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Therefore, the conclusion must be reviewed again.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 그러나 핵심 주장은 유지할 수 있습니다.
dialogue.romanization: geureona haeksim jujangeun yujihal su itseumnida.
dialogue.en: However, the main claim can be maintained.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: By contrast, the case analysis needs strengthening.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 한편 예상되는 반론도 따로 검토해야 합니다.
dialogue.romanization: hanpyeon yesangdoeneun ballondo ttaro geomtohaeya hamnida.
dialogue.en: Meanwhile, the expected counterarguments must also be reviewed separately.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 즉, 결론보다 근거와 논리를 보완해야 합니다.
dialogue.romanization: jeuk, gyeollonboda geungeowa nollireul bowanhaeya hamnida.
dialogue.en: In other words, the evidence and reasoning need more work than the conclusion.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 결국 보고서는 주장, 근거, 사례가 서로 연결되어야 합니다.
dialogue.romanization: gyeolguk bogoseoneun jujang, geungeo, saryega seoro yeongyeoldoeeoya hamnida.
dialogue.en: Ultimately, a report's claim, evidence, and cases must be connected.

chapters.guidedPractice: Revise a weak report paragraph: add one sentence with 따라서, one contrast with 그러나 or 반면에, one clarification with 즉, and one final synthesis with 결국.
chapters.realLifeTask: Write four formal sentences using two connectors such as 따라서, 그러나, 즉, or 결국.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner gives you a claim and two pieces of evidence; decide whether the conclusion, evidence, logic, or counterargument needs revision.
chapters.review: Can you explain why 따라서, 그러나, 반면에, 한편, 즉, and 결국 cannot be swapped freely in a formal paragraph?

beginnerGuide.title: Register first
beginnerGuide.body: This chapter is about written reasoning, not casual conversation. A paragraph with 따라서 or 그러나 should usually keep formal endings such as -다, -한다, -이다, or formal polite -습니다.

beginnerGuide.title: Connector roles
beginnerGuide.body: Use 따라서 for a conclusion from evidence, 그러나 for direct contrast, 반면에 for two-sided comparison, 한편 for a parallel development, 즉 for restatement, and 결국 for final synthesis.

beginnerGuide.title: Argument vocabulary
beginnerGuide.body: Read 근거, 결론, 핵심, 논리, 사례, and 반론 as one set. These words let you diagnose what is weak in a report instead of only saying the Korean is difficult.

checkpoints: I can choose a connector that matches the relationship between sentences.
I can keep formal connectors and formal endings in the same register.
I can revise a paragraph so the reader can follow the claim and reason.

chapters.title: Written Connectives and Nominalisation — -(으)며, -(으)나, -(으)므로, -고자, -(으)ㅁ
chapters.goal: Join clauses inside one sentence the way notices and reports do.
chapters.scenario: You are editing a notice that reads as a string of short sentences glued together with 그리고 and 그래서.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 공지문이 너무 짧은 문장만 이어져서 읽기 불편해요.
dialogue.romanization: gongjimuni neomu jjalbeun munjangman ieojyeoseo ilgi bulpyeonhaeyo.
dialogue.en: The notice is nothing but short sentences, so it's awkward to read.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 문장 안에서 이어 주는 어미를 쓰면 됩니다. '-며'나 '-나' 같은 거요.
dialogue.romanization: munjang aneseo ieo juneun eomireul sseumyeon doemnida. '-myeo'na '-na' gateun geoyo.
dialogue.en: Use the endings that join clauses inside a sentence — things like -며 and -나.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: And when I need to give a reason?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Use -으므로. Don't mix it up with -ㅁ으로써, which means 'by means of'.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 그럼 마지막 줄은 '-기 바람'으로 닫으면 되겠네요.
dialogue.romanization: geureom majimak jureun '-gi baram'euro dadeumyeon doegenneyo.
dialogue.en: Then I can close the last line with -기 바람.

chapters.guidedPractice: Take a paragraph of your own writing that uses 그리고, 그래서, and 하지만 between sentences. Rewrite it so each pair becomes one sentence joined by -(으)며, -(으)므로, or -(으)나.
chapters.realLifeTask: Write a five-line notice using -(으)며, -(으)나, -(으)므로, -고자, and a closing -기 바람.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner reads you two short sentences. You join them into one, choosing the ending that matches the relationship between them.
chapters.review: Can you explain the difference between -(으)므로 and -(으)ㅁ으로써, and between -(으)ㅁ and -기?

beginnerGuide.title: Two layers, not one
beginnerGuide.body: 따라서 and 그러나 join sentence to sentence. -(으)며 and -(으)나 join clause to clause inside a single sentence. Formal writing uses both at once, and a paragraph that only has the first layer reads choppy.

beginnerGuide.title: The 으 is not decoration
beginnerGuide.body: -(으)며, -(으)나, and -(으)므로 all add 으 only after a consonant. 비싸다 gives 비싸나, not 비싸으나. And a ㄹ-stem drops its ㄹ before -(으)나 because that ending starts with ㄴ: 열다 becomes 여나.

beginnerGuide.title: Notices stop on a noun
beginnerGuide.body: Public notices close their lines with -(으)ㅁ or -기 바람 instead of a polite ending: 취소될 수 있음, 제출하기 바람. It is a register, not rudeness — nobody in particular is speaking.

checkpoints: I can join two clauses inside one sentence instead of starting a new one.
I can add 으 only after a consonant, and drop ㄹ before -(으)나.
I can close a notice line with -(으)ㅁ or -기 바람.

chapters.title: Reading News and Notices — Passives, -적/-화/-성, and Headlines
chapters.goal: Read a Korean headline and the article under it without stalling.
chapters.scenario: You open a news app and the headline has no particles, no verb, and three Sino-Korean suffixes.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 이 헤드라인 무슨 뜻이에요? 조사가 없어서 모르겠어요.
dialogue.romanization: i hedeurain museun tteusieyo? josaga eopseoseo moreugesseoyo.
dialogue.en: What does this headline mean? There are no particles, so I can't tell.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 뒤에서부터 읽으세요. 마지막 명사가 동사 역할을 해요.
dialogue.romanization: dwieseobuteo ilgeuseyo. majimak myeongsaga dongsa yeokareul haeyo.
dialogue.en: Read it from the back. The last noun is doing the work of the verb.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Ah, so 확대 was 확대한다.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Right. In the body it appears as 확대된다, because the subject is the thing being expanded.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: It also says 알려졌다 — that means it isn't confirmed, right?

chapters.guidedPractice: Take three headlines from a Korean news app and unpack each one into a full sentence: restore the verb from the final noun, then the object particle, then the topic particle.
chapters.realLifeTask: Write a three-line news item: a headline with particles dropped, a sentence citing a source, and a forecast.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner reads a headline aloud. You say the full sentence it stands for, with every particle back in place.
chapters.review: Can you rank 확인됐다, 밝혀졌다, and 알려졌다 by how confirmed the claim is?

beginnerGuide.title: Read the headline backwards
beginnerGuide.body: The last noun is the verb: 확대 means 확대한다 or 확대된다. The noun before it is usually the object, so put 을/를 back. Whatever sits before the comma is the topic, so put 은/는 back.

beginnerGuide.title: The passive tells you how sure the writer is
beginnerGuide.body: 확인됐다 is verified, 밝혀졌다 was uncovered by an investigation, and 알려졌다 is secondhand and unconfirmed. Translating all three as 'it is said' throws away the whole scale.

beginnerGuide.title: Three suffixes build most of the vocabulary
beginnerGuide.body: -적 makes a modifier (경제적 부담), -화 makes a process (자동화되다), and -성 makes an abstract noun with fixed partners (가능성이 높다, 필요성이 크다). Learn the partners as chunks.

checkpoints: I can restore the dropped particles and the deleted verb in a headline.
I can tell how confirmed a claim is from which passive the writer chose.
I can build and read -적, -화, and -성 words with their usual partners.

chapters.title: Body-Part Idioms and Proverbs — 손이 크다, 발이 넓다, 티끌 모아 태산
chapters.goal: Describe someone's character the way Koreans actually do.
chapters.scenario: A friend asks what the new colleague is like, and every honest answer turns out to involve a body part.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: What's the new person like?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 발이 넓으신 것 같아요. 벌써 다들 아시더라고요.
dialogue.romanization: bari neolbeusin geot gatayo. beolsseo dadeul asideoragoyo.
dialogue.en: Very well connected, I think. She already knows everyone.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: And discreet? Would it be okay to tell her something private?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 입이 무거우신 편이에요. 걱정 안 하셔도 돼요.
dialogue.romanization: ibi mugeousin pyeonieyo. geokjeong an hasyeodo dwaeyo.
dialogue.en: She's on the discreet side. You don't need to worry.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 다행이네요. 저는 귀가 얇아서 아무 말이나 다 믿거든요.
dialogue.romanization: dahaengineyo. jeoneun gwiga yalbaseo amu marina da mitgeodeunyo.
dialogue.en: That's a relief. I'm so easily swayed that I believe anything I'm told.

chapters.guidedPractice: Think of five people you know and describe each one with a body-part idiom instead of an adjective. Say each sentence out loud in its clause shape: [body part]이/가 [adjective].
chapters.realLifeTask: Describe three people using body-part idioms, then close with a proverb that fits one of them.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner describes a personality in plain words. You give the idiom that says the same thing in one clause.
chapters.review: Can you say why 큰 손이에요 is wrong, and why 귀가 얇다 has nothing to do with hearing?

beginnerGuide.title: It is a clause, not a phrase
beginnerGuide.body: English would say 'a generous hand'. Korean says 손이 크다 — the body part takes 이/가 and the adjective carries the ending. Keep 손이 크세요, 발이 넓으세요, 눈이 높으세요 in that shape.

beginnerGuide.title: Two of them are passives
beginnerGuide.body: 발이 묶이다 means you were stranded by something else, and 눈에 띄다 means the thing caught your eye by itself. So it is 발이 묶였어요, not 발을 묶었어요, and 눈에 띄다, not 눈을 띄다.

beginnerGuide.title: Quote proverbs whole
beginnerGuide.body: 티끌 모아 태산 keeps its bare nouns with no particles. Attach the grammar on the outside: 태산이에요, 태산이라고, or 천 리 간다더니. Never rebuild the proverb into a new sentence.

checkpoints: I can keep a body-part idiom in its clause shape.
I can use 발이 묶이다 and 눈에 띄다 with the right particles.
I can quote a proverb whole and attach 이다, -이라고, or -다더니 to it.

exitTask.canDo: Describe someone's character the way Koreans actually do.
exitTask.prompt: Describe three people using body-part idioms, then close with a proverb that fits one of them.

sampleAnswer.ko: 우리 어머니는 손이 크셔서 명절마다 음식이 남아요. 친구 지훈이는 발이 넓어서 모르는 사람이 없고요. 저는 귀가 얇아서 광고만 보면 다 사고 싶어져요. 그래도 티끌 모아 태산이라고 조금씩 모으고 있어요.
sampleAnswer.en: My mother cooks on such a scale that there are leftovers every holiday. My friend Jihoon is so well connected there's nobody he doesn't know. I'm easily swayed and want to buy everything I see advertised. Still, little by little makes a lot, so I'm saving bit by bit.

checklist: I can keep a body-part idiom in its clause shape.
I can use 발이 묶이다 and 눈에 띄다 with the right particles.
I can quote a proverb whole and attach 이다, -이라고, or -다더니 to it.
Make it about your real day: your name, place, time, or plan.
Keep the first version short before you make it longer.

chapters.title: Synthesis and Production Review
chapters.goal: Put the whole course together in one message that fits the situation.
chapters.scenario: You switch between an interview answer, a formal email, coworker chat, and a KakaoTalk reply.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 오늘 면접 답변, 이메일, 카톡 답장을 한 번에 검수해 볼까요?
dialogue.romanization: oneul myeonjeop dapbyeon, imeil, katok dapjangeul han beone geomsuhae bolkkayo?
dialogue.en: Shall we review today's interview answer, email, and KakaoTalk reply together?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 먼저 상황과 상대방을 정하고 문체를 맞춰야 해요.
dialogue.romanization: meonjeo sanghwanggwa sangdaebangeul jeonghago munchereul matchwoya haeyo.
dialogue.en: First, decide the situation and listener, then match the style.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 면접 답변은 높임말과 시제를 확인하고, 이메일은 연결어와 마무리를 봐요.
dialogue.romanization: myeonjeop dapbyeoneun nopimmalgwa sijereul hwaginhago, imeireun yeongyeoreowa mamurireul bwayo.
dialogue.en: For the interview answer, check honorifics and tense; for the email, check connectors and the closing.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 카톡에서는 편하게 써도 되지만 회사 메일에는 ㅋㅋ를 빼야 해요.
dialogue.romanization: katogeseoneun pyeonhage sseodo doejiman hoesa meileneun kkreul ppaeya haeyo.
dialogue.en: You can write casually in KakaoTalk, but in a company email you need to remove ㅋㅋ.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Lastly, I will check even each particle again.

chapters.guidedPractice: Choose one idea and produce it four ways: interview answer, formal email, coworker chat, and friend KakaoTalk. Check situation, listener, style, particles, tense, and connectors each time.
chapters.realLifeTask: Rewrite one idea for two different listeners, then check register, particles, tense, connectors, and closing.
chapters.friendPractice: A partner gives you a task and relationship. Say whether you need casual, polite, or formal Korean, then produce and revise one sentence.
chapters.review: Can you switch the same message between interview, email, coworker talk, and friend chat without leaving mismatched particles, tense, connectors, or slang?

beginnerGuide.title: Start with the situation
beginnerGuide.body: Do not start by translating English. First decide the purpose, listener, and channel: interview, email, coworker chat, or friend KakaoTalk.

beginnerGuide.title: Check five layers
beginnerGuide.body: After drafting, check 문체, 입자, 시제, 높임말, and 연결어. A sentence can have good vocabulary and still fail because one layer does not match the situation.

beginnerGuide.title: Rewrite, not decorate
beginnerGuide.body: Polite Korean is not casual Korean with 요 added. Rewrite rough slang, sentence endings, connectors, and closing phrases together.

checkpoints: I can choose the register before choosing vocabulary or endings.
I can check particles, tense, honorifics, connector, and closing in one pass.
I can rewrite the same meaning for formal email and casual chat.
